entry.title: Play with the things already here
entry.summary: Davies makes room at home for open-ended play as well as practical activities. Familiar favorites can be a good place to begin.
entry.cue: Your child may be exploring a toy in a new way or acting out something from ordinary life.
detail: She describes pretend play as one way children process what they experience: cooking, caring for a baby, or taking a trip. It need not become a lesson or a performance for an adult.

Her home examples include blocks, farm animals, trains, and vehicles. These are possibilities within a varied collection, not a shopping list. Materials still need to fit the child using them, with supervision for small parts.
If a child attends a Montessori classroom, she makes room at home for daily life, outdoors, creativity, and rest without duplicating all the school materials.
